prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: [验证] 中英混排 · 会议待办 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "#" · longest unbreakable word 11px · one-line width 11px
  col 2: header "Action item" · longest unbreakable word 87px · one-line width 536px
  col 3: header "负责人" · longest unbreakable word 33px · one-line width 53px
  col 4: header "Due" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 5: header "状态" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 53px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 480px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 479px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"bad","why":"The action column is far too narrow: English words break within words, rows become very tall, and the short fields have excessive space."},"B":{"grade":"good","why":"The action items read comfortably and dates and statuses stay intact, but the 负责人 header wraps onto two lines."},"C":{"grade":"poor","why":"The wide action column leaves the status column so narrow that its header and values stack character by character, making scanning difficult."},"D":{"grade":"excellent","why":"The columns are well balanced: headers, names, dates and statuses stay intact, while action items wrap naturally and rows remain easy to scan."},"E":{"grade":"poor","why":"The owner header stacks vertically, and a name, a date and status values break across lines, weakening row-by-row comparison."},"F":{"grade":"excellent","why":"The action items wrap naturally, and the compact columns keep headers and short values intact with a clear, consistent row rhythm."}},"best":["D","F"],"confidence":"high","unsure":"D and F are very close visually; their small width differences do not produce a clear advantage in the rendered table."}
